_readme.trainingPair: TRAINING PAIR (folded in v20.9): Phase 1 (trainee learning) — put the TRAINEE in the Driver slot? No: put the qualified TRAINER as Driver and the TRAINEE (who is a helper-level learner) in the Helper slot as usual. Phase 2 (trainee can drive) — put the TRAINEE as Driver and the qualified TRAINER as Helper: the Helper dropdown now also lists DRIVERS (tagged '(driver-guide)'), and a driver placed in the Helper slot COUNTS AS A FULL GUIDE (satisfies needsGuide, clears the NEEDS GUIDE flag). Crew line renders 'Driver - Helper' as normal (e.g. 'Racel - Miarfy'). Base-pass/ability checks still apply to the person in the DRIVER slot only. NOTE: if you want the guiding driver's own base pass checked too, or special WhatsApp wording like '(training)', say so.

If projectedFinish > close -> Resolve/Review flag 'won't reach [site] before [close]'. Currently the hours are ESTIMATES (flagged _estNote) and the check is not yet wired to the row — enable via CFG.dumpTime.enabled once rolling actuals arrive.

_readme.cfgVersionExplained: cfgVersion format = YYMMDD-NN (settings snapshot date + increment). '260720-89' = the 89th settings build stamped 2026-07-20. It tracks the DATA/settings snapshot; the app code version is the separate 'v21.38' in the header. They move independently: editing settings bumps cfg; new features bump the app version.
designPrinciples: Our design principles (internal notes for how we build this):

1) SEPARATE DATA FROM CODE. All our specifics (people, equipment, routes, rates, passes, estimates) live in ONE editable config object exported as a single JSON = our portable source of truth. The HTML stays generic; the JSON carries the data.

2) MODEL DIMENSIONS INDEPENDENTLY, DON'T HARDCODE. Route, truck, driver, helper, day, and base/site permit are each their own list with per-day overrides (start times, bases, helper-needed, estimates). Adding a route or a rule never means touching logic.

3) DEFAULTS + REASONED EXCEPTIONS. Everything usual is pre-filled (usual routes, usual bases, projected hours); any deviation is allowed but REQUIRES a logged reason — captures the why for audit without slowing the normal case.

4) VALIDATE, DON'T BLOCK BLINDLY. Three tiers — hard errors that block posting (missing driver, expired required permit, same-time double-book), soft warnings to confirm (unusual day, 2+ shifts), and routine checklist items. Guardrails, not handcuffs.

5) OUTPUT IS A VIEW OF THE DATA. The WhatsApp/Kakao drafts are generated from the same model, gated behind an explicit Generate so a draft is never silently stale. Crew vs office = two renderers off one source.

6) PROJECT FORWARD, RECONCILE WITH ACTUALS. Hours/cost start as estimates and are overwritten by real numbers as they arrive (manual now, timesheet-automation later). The 40h OT threshold + cost fall out of the same running model.

7) NON-CODER-EDITABLE + OFFLINE. Every setting is editable in-app; sandbox-safe custom dialogs (no native alert/confirm); persists in localStorage; optional static hosting (GitHub Pages) with fetch-latest so one URL serves everyone — no backend, no login.

8) PLAN THESE INPUTS EARLY (hardest to backfill): per-person/route/day familiarity + guide rules; per-person availability constraints; real duration + speed per route/day; permit/credential expiries; pay rates incl. multi-employer OT.

versionLog.feat: Standby route + reasons; expired/missing REQUIRED base pass LOCKS the row until fixed; review checklist popup (Resolve / Review / Routine).
versionLog.note: BIG TROUBLESHOOT #1: the lock dialog + Reset/Clear buttons silently did nothing. Root cause: the SharePoint/preview SANDBOX BLOCKS native alert() and confirm(). Fix = custom in-page modal (showDialog/showConfirm). AVOID native alert/confirm entirely. Also fixed a lock that used pointer-events:none which killed the click-guard AND the escape hatch — greying must be visual only (.lockgrey), events stay live.

versionLog.feat: Flag-bubble system (double-book, needs-guide, no-driver) pinned above each field; grouped Resolve by route; excluded-from-schedule multiselect→checkbox list.
versionLog.note: BIG TROUBLESHOOT #2: a refactor deleted wrap.appendChild(top) so the field row never rendered → 'Cannot read addEventListener of null' → whole page failed to load. Lesson: after moving markup, confirm the container is still appended. Bubble layout churned a lot (overlap, wrapping, stacking) before settling on fixed max-width chips that wrap their own text; don't let one field's bubble overflow into the neighbour.

Helper-wash UI went through several formats (checkbox broke row height) before landing as a compact chip / in-Helper-label toggle.
